methods: deriving a polynomial for a special sine
statement:
If $\theta+\phi+\psi=\tfrac12\pi$, show that
$$\sin^2\theta+\sin^2\phi+\sin^2\psi+2\sin\theta\sin\phi\sin\psi=1.$$

By taking $\theta=\phi=\tfrac15\pi$ in this equation, or otherwise, show that $\sin\tfrac1{10}\pi$ satisfies the equation
$$8x^3+8x^2-1=0.$$
solution:
Since $\psi=\tfrac\pi2-(\theta+\phi)$, we have $\sin\psi=\cos(\theta+\phi)$ and $\cos\psi=\sin(\theta+\phi)$. The identity
$$\sin^2\theta+\sin^2\phi+\sin^2\psi+2\sin\theta\sin\phi\sin\psi=1$$
follows by expanding $\sin\psi=\cos\theta\cos\phi-\sin\theta\sin\phi$ and simplifying (equivalently, it is the identity $\cos^2(\theta+\phi)+\sin^2(\theta+\phi)=1$ after rearrangement).

**Special case.** Put $\theta=\phi=\tfrac\pi5$, so $\psi=\tfrac\pi2-\tfrac{2\pi}{5}=\tfrac\pi{10}$. Let $x=\sin\tfrac\pi{10}$. The identity gives
$$2\sin^2\tfrac\pi5+x^2+2x\sin^2\tfrac\pi5=1.$$
Now $\sin\tfrac\pi5=\sin(2\cdot\tfrac\pi{10})=2\sin\tfrac\pi{10}\cos\tfrac\pi{10}=2x\sqrt{1-x^2}$, so $\sin^2\tfrac\pi5=4x^2(1-x^2)$. Substituting:
$$8x^2(1-x^2)+x^2+8x^3(1-x^2)=1,$$
i.e. $9x^2+8x^3-8x^4-8x^5=1$, or
$$-8x^5-8x^4+8x^3+9x^2-1=0.$$
This factors as
$$(8x^3+8x^2-1)(1-x^2)=0.$$
Since $x=\sin\tfrac\pi{10}\neq\pm1$, we have $1-x^2\neq0$, and therefore
$$8x^3+8x^2-1=0.$$
Thus $\sin\tfrac\pi{10}$ satisfies $8x^3+8x^2-1=0$.
hints: Use sin ψ = cos(θ+φ) and expand.
Substitute θ=φ=π/5 so that ψ=π/10, and write sin(π/5) in terms of x=sin(π/10).
